 8th Pay Commission Salary Hike In 2027: 4 Fitment Factor May Mean Rs 15.20 Lakh Arrears at Rs 53,100 Basic Pay
 Personal Finance oi-Pooja Jaiswar By Pooja Jaiswar 
 Updated: Thursday, November 12, 2026, 10:10 [IST]
 Add as a preferred source on Google The final report for 8th Pay Commission is expected to be submitted in May 2027, which will give more clarity on its implementation date. More than 1.17 crore central government employees and pensioners expect the 8th CPC recommendations to be implemented anytime in late 2027, while the effective date counting will likely be from January 1, 2026, as the 7th Pay Commission ended on December 31, 2025. If this happens, the central government could enjoy more than 12 months' arrears. However, the fitment factor will be crucial for revised salary, pensions, and arrear benefits, and it will vary from employee to employee.
 8th Pay Commission Salary Hike In 2026?
 The term of reference (ToR) formed on November 3, 2025, compiling of chairman Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai, part-time member Professor Pulak Ghosh, and member secretary Pankaj, is given the responsibility to articulate a full-fledged recommendations report for the 8th Pay Commission. They are given 18 months time period to submit the final report.
 The ToR led by Desai has the task of examining and recommending changes that are desirable and feasible in the emoluments, including pay, allowances, and other facilities/benefits, in cash or kind, having regard to rationalization, contemporary functional requirements, and the specialized needs of various departments, agencies, and services.
 The goal of 8th CPC is to improve the cost of living of employees and retirees.
 But the final report submission date is not the implementation date, and there is no guarantee that 8th CPC will be implemented in 2027. The government will take a call after reviewing, evaluating, and approving the final report of the 8th Pay Commission.
 8th Pay Commission Implementation Date:
 The history of the past 3 pay commissions shows that it has taken at least 4 months to 8 months' time to approve the final report to implement the commissions.
 For instance, the final report for the 5th Pay Commission was submitted on January 30, 1997; the government approved the report on October 24, 1997—around an 8-month and 24-day time period was taken. The effective date was January 1, 1996.
 In case of 6th CPC, the final report was submitted on March 24, 2008 and the approval came after 4 months 21 days on August 14, 2008. The effective date was January 1, 2006.
 Meanwhile, in the case of 7th Pay Commission, the final report was submitted on November 19, 2015 and the approval came after around 7 months 10 days. The effective date was January 1, 2016.
 If we go by the 7th Pay Commission timeline, the probability of 8th Pay Commission getting implemented in December 2027 emerges. If we take the 6th Pay Commission timeline, the probability for 8th CPC emerges in October 2027. And if the government took over 8 months like 5th CPC, then the likelihood of implementing 8th CPC is high in January to February 2028.
 Particulars 5th CPC 6th CPC 7th CPC 
 Final report submitted January 30, 1997 March 24, 2008 November 19, 2015 
 Government/Cabinet approval October 24, 1997 August 14, 2008 June 29, 2016 
 Time from report to approval Around 8 months 24 days Around 4 months 21 days Around 7 months 10 days 
 Effective date of revised pay January 1, 1996 January 1, 2006 January 1, 2016 
 Arrears payable from January 1, 1996 January 1, 2006 January 1, 2016 
 Experts believe that 8th CPC will be implemented in financial year 2027-28. As per Monarch Networth Capital, the key theme for Samvat 2083 is the 8th Pay Commission.
 The brokerage's note added, "We expect its recommendations to be accepted in FY28, putting more money in the hands of over 2 crore employees and pensioners. Past commissions saw the extra income flow towards automobiles, travel and tourism, premium beverages, and consumer durables, and we expect a similar pattern. The premiumization theme could benefit these consumption and discretionary pockets."
 Assuming that the effective date is decided on January 1, 2026, then central government employees are in for hefty arrears. Let's calculate:
 8th Pay Commission Fitment Factor
 Notably, a lot will depend upon the fitment factor, which is crucial in calculating the scope of hikes in basic pay and pensions from 7th CPC. There are many recommendations for fitment factor. Some are modest at 1.90, and some recommendations are extraordinarily eye-popping, like the 4 fitment factors.

 Let's assume that the government decides to settle for 4 fitment factor for 8th CPC.
 A fitment factor of 4 translates into a whopping 300% surge in basic pay mathematically from level 1 to level 18 graded central government employees.
 8th Pay Commission Salary Hike
 Formula to calculate revised basic pay:
 {8th CPC Basic Pay}= {7th CPC Basic Pay} X 4
 Let's take level 9 grade employees; The current basic salary under 7th CPC is at Rs 53,100. If fitment factor 4 is approved, the salary would rise by 300% to Rs 2,12,400 per month.
 Level 9: Estimated 8th CPC Basic Pay = Rs 53,100 x 4 = Rs 2,12,400.
 Level 1: The salary of level 1 employees will rise by 300% to Rs 72,000 from Rs 18,000.
 Level 5: The basic salary for this grade will rise to Rs 1,16,800 per month from Rs 29,200 per month.
 Level 10: This grade level employees will receive Rs 2,24,400 per month from their basic pay of Rs 56,100 per month if fitment is fixed at 4.
 Level 15: The basic salary in 8th CPC will rise to Rs 7,28,800 per month for this grade employees from the current Rs 1,82,200 per month.
 8th Pay Commission Arrears:
 The formula for calculating areas is:
 The arrears calculation formula is (New Salary - Old Salary) × Months Due
 The arrears calculation also includes dearness allowance (DA) component. If we take the level 9 employees grade, the difference between the new salary under 8th CPC and old salary of 7th CPC would fall at Rs 1,59,300 per month.
 For January to June 2026, the DA was at 60% and then hiked to 63% from July to December 2026. Let's apply that as well. Calculation:
 Revised Basic Pay = Rs 2,12,400 
Old Basic Pay = Rs 53,100
January - June 2026 DA = 60% 
July - December 2026 DA = 63%
 For, January to June - DA at 60%, the monthly difference will be Rs 1,27,440 per month. For July to December - DA at 63%, the monthly difference will come around Rs 1,25,847.
 Arrears for January to March 2026 = Rs x 6 months = Rs 7,64,640
 Arrears for July - December 2026 = Rs 42,206 x 6 months = Rs 7,55,082.
 Arrears for entire 12 months (January - December 2026) would come around Rs 15,19,722 for the employee.
